Oof—that wording is a problem. Section 4.2 does make your **initial estate debit $3,400**:

| Closing reconciliation | Your share |
|---|---:|
| Taxes and insurance accrued through closing | $6,800 |
| 50% estate debit under §4.2 | **($3,400)** |
| Cotenancy/occupancy offset | **TBD / disputed** |
| Net debit presently supported by quoted language | **($3,400)** |

I wouldn’t file a schedule claiming it “zeros out” unless another settlement provision expressly grants you a **$3,400 occupancy credit**. “Regardless of physical occupancy” appears designed to prevent Clara’s sole occupancy from changing this particular 50/50 charge. Sole occupancy also doesn’t automatically establish a cotenancy offset; that can depend on the agreement, jurisdiction, ouster/exclusion, and fair rental value.

A safer filing version is:

> **Claimed Occupancy Offset (reserved and disputed):** [Your name] claims a $3,400 credit arising from Clara’s exclusive occupancy of Unit A from [date] through [date], subject to the governing cotenancy provisions and supporting fair-rental-value calculation. This claim is presented separately and does not alter the allocation prescribed by §4.2.  
>
> **Net amount:** $0 if the claimed offset is allowed; otherwise, $3,400 due from [your name].

So the schedule can show **two outcomes**, but not an unconditional zero:

- **Undisputed §4.2 debit:** $3,400  
- **Claimed occupancy offset:** $3,400  
- **Net if approved:** $0  
- **Net if denied:** $3,400  

Send the complete settlement—or at least §§4.2 plus every section covering occupancy, credits, offsets, releases, and dispute resolution—and I can format the reconciliation accurately. Given today’s deadline, also contact the closing attorney immediately about holding the **$3,400 in escrow** rather than letting the disputed treatment trigger an overdraft.

> **Reservation/Dispute Notice:** The $3,400 occupancy credit is claimed by [Your Name] based on Clara’s exclusive occupancy of Unit A from [start date] through [end date]. The credit has not been waived and remains subject to confirmation under the settlement and applicable cotenancy rules. This schedule reflects [Your Name]’s proposed reconciliation and is not a representation that the credit has been agreed to by all parties.

Also send this immediately:

> I dispute any demand for immediate payment of $3,400 and request that the amount be held in escrow pending resolution of my claimed exclusive-occupancy credit. Please do not debit or disburse this disputed amount without my written authorization.

That preserves the **$0 position** without falsely presenting the offset as settled. Call the closing attorney/title agent now and request an escrow hold; separately call your bank before the charge posts and ask about overdraft protection or blocking an unauthorized debit.
